engine_note: Evals: Stockfish 19 lite, single thread, depth 14 per move, cp from the mover's view; win_pct_drop uses the Lichess win% curve. Mechanisms checked with depth-18 lines. Expect small numeric differences from deeper engines; labels are what matter.

label_definitions.threat_ignored: A piece was already attacked (by the opponent's last move) and the player's move does not deal with it.
label_definitions.hanging_piece: A piece/pawn moved to or left on a square where it can be captured for free immediately, with no tactic needed.
label_definitions.defended_target_grab: Capturing something that is defended, so the capturing piece is lost (e.g. bishop takes a knight-defended pawn).
label_definitions.removed_defender: The moved unit (piece or pawn) was the only defender of another unit/square that becomes capturable.
label_definitions.discovered_attack_allowed: Opponent moves a blocking piece (often with its own threat/check), uncovering an attack by a long-range piece behind it.
label_definitions.discovered_attack_missed: Player had a discovered attack available and did not play it.
label_definitions.in_between_move: Opponent inserts a forcing move (check or queen attack) before recapturing.
label_definitions.fork_allowed: Opponent can attack two or more valuable units with one move (knight forks most common).
label_definitions.fork_missed: Player had a fork available and did not play it.
label_definitions.pawn_fork_allowed: A pawn advance attacks two pieces at once.
label_definitions.skewer_allowed: King (or queen) and another piece on one line; check/attack on the front piece wins the back piece.
label_definitions.back_rank_mate_allowed: Mate (or decisive loss) on the back rank because the king has no luft.
label_definitions.mate_missed: A mate (usually in 1-3) was available and not played.
label_definitions.free_capture_missed: An undefended enemy piece was capturable (often far along a queen/bishop/rook line) and was not taken.
label_definitions.missed_bigger_capture: Player took material but a different capture won more (or kept key defenders).
label_definitions.pin_exploit_missed: An enemy piece was pinned and could be attacked (often by a pawn) but wasn't.
label_definitions.trapped_piece: Player's own piece has no safe retreat and gets trapped.
label_definitions.trapped_piece_risk: Player's queen/piece is deep in enemy territory with very few escape squares and the opponent has a move that would trap or win it.
label_definitions.opened_line_to_own_king: A capture/move opens a file or diagonal toward the player's own king.
label_definitions.opened_line_to_own_queen: Moving a blocker (often a pawn capture) opens a line from an enemy piece to the player's queen.
label_definitions.greedy_queen_raid: Queen leaves the defense to grab distant material, exposing the king.
label_definitions.check_blocked_with_tempo: A check that the opponent blocks with a move that also attacks the checking piece.
label_definitions.incomplete_exchange: Player failed to recapture/complete a trade and ended up a piece down.
label_definitions.unsound_sacrifice: Material sacrifice without enough attackers to follow up.
label_definitions.castled_into_attack: Castling into an existing pin and/or pawn storm.
label_definitions.promotion_square_covered: Promoting on a square the opponent controls.
label_definitions.opening_structure_error: Opening move that misreads the pawn structure (e.g. wrong pawn break for the line played).

usage: Run the app's analysis + detectors on each game in games[]; for each moment, compare the detector's primary label (and lesson) to primary_label/secondary_labels.
Score: exact primary match = 1, match to a secondary label = 0.5, otherwise 0. Report per-label precision/recall and overall accuracy.
Any label listed in must_not_label for a moment counts as a hard failure if it is the primary label/lesson the app produces.
Tune only on split=="tune"; report holdout accuracy separately. Do not hard-code game-specific rules.
clean_games: the app must not produce a lesson listed in must_not_lesson.
If a detector cannot explain a moment, "unclassified" scores 0 but is NOT a hard failure (better than a wrong generic label).

moments.mechanism: Rook captured the g4 pawn, which was defended by the f3 bishop; 29.Bxg4 wins the rook for a pawn.
moments.expected_lesson: Count a target's defenders before capturing it.

moments.mechanism: Leaves the back rank defended only by the rooks: Qxb8+ Rxb8 Rd8+ Rxd8 Rxd8# (mate in 3).
moments.expected_lesson: Give the king an escape square (luft) and watch back-rank checks.

moments.mechanism: King on h1 has no escape squares; 42...Rh3# is mate.
moments.expected_lesson: Before each move in an ending with rooks, check whether the enemy rook has a mating check.

moments.mechanism: 17.Nxe6! moves the d4 knight off the d-file, uncovering the d1 rook onto the d6 queen while the knight hits g7/c7.
moments.expected_lesson: When a piece stands between your long-range piece and their queen/king, look at every move of that piece.

moments.mechanism: Taking b5 with the queen (king castled queenside) allows 27...Rab8! and Qxb2+. Needs depth >= 18 to see (depth 14 rates it as small).
moments.expected_lesson: Before grabbing material, check whether the capture opens a file/diagonal toward your own king.

moments.mechanism: Bishop left d6 (stopped guarding e7). 31.Ne7+ moves the c6 knight with check and uncovers Qd5 onto the a8 rook. 30...Re8+ was winning.
moments.expected_lesson: A knight check that uncovers a queen line wins material: check what a moving enemy piece uncovers, and what your moved piece was guarding.

moments.mechanism: Bishop moved to g4, where the queen captures it (Qxg4) and nothing defends it.
moments.expected_lesson: Before letting go, check if the destination square is attacked and undefended.

moments.mechanism: The e1 rook was already attacked by the king on f2 (after 16...Re1+ 17.Kf2) and nothing defended it. 17...Qb6+ is a check but does not save the rook: Kxe1 wins it. 17...Qxf3+ was best (trade queens with check, then the rook can get away). White missed it in the game (18.Kg3).
moments.expected_lesson: Before making your own move, ask what the opponent's last move attacks.

moments.mechanism: 13.Bg3 blocks the check while attacking the queen; the queen ends up misplaced.
moments.expected_lesson: Before giving a check, look for blocks that come with tempo.

moments.mechanism: 32...Ng5 forks the f3 queen, h3 bishop and e4 rook.
moments.expected_lesson: Check every square an enemy knight can reach next move.

moments.mechanism: The f3 queen was the only defender of the h3 bishop; after Qe2, Qxh3.
moments.expected_lesson: Ask what the moving piece was defending.

moments.mechanism: Queen and king end up on the 2nd rank: Qh1+ Ke2 Qxh2+ and Qxa2.
moments.expected_lesson: Never leave your king and queen on the same line an enemy queen/rook can reach.

moments.mechanism: 24.Bxa8 won a rook and kept the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal; Bxa6 took a knight and left the diagonal/f3 square, letting Black counterattack.
moments.expected_lesson: Compare all captures; prefer the one that keeps key defenders in place.

moments.mechanism: Qa4 attacked the undefended f4 bishop along the 4th rank (also on move 13). 14...Qxf4 wins a piece.
moments.expected_lesson: After every move, trace your queen's lines (ranks, files, diagonals) to the end.

moments.mechanism: Rf1 leaves the d7 knight to Rxd7. 22...Rh6 would have trapped the queen on h7.
moments.expected_lesson: Check which of your pieces are undefended after the move; look for trapping the enemy queen.

moments.mechanism: King steps onto the 6th rank with its own rook on e6: Ra6+ skewers and wins the rook in a drawn R vs R ending.
moments.expected_lesson: In endgames, keep king and pieces off the same line the enemy rook can reach.

moments.mechanism: The a6 pawn was the only defender of b5; after a5, Nxb5.
moments.expected_lesson: Pawns are defenders too: ask what a pawn was guarding before pushing it.

moments.mechanism: After 13...Bxg5 14.Nd6+ Kf8, White must recapture with 15.Nxg5; Qb4 lets ...Be7 save the bishop: White is a piece down.
moments.expected_lesson: Finish a trade before starting a new idea; recount material after captures and checks.

moments.mechanism: Bishop on e4 has no retreat (d3 pawn, f3 knight block it); 10...f5 traps it (Bd5+ cxd5).
moments.expected_lesson: Before placing a piece forward, check it has a way back.

moments.mechanism: After g3 but before Bg2, the h1 rook is exposed to the queen on d5: 4...Qxh1.
moments.expected_lesson: Between g3 and Bg2, block or occupy the long diagonal.

moments.mechanism: Bishop sacrifice on h6 with too few attackers ready to follow up (queen on d1, knight inactive).
moments.expected_lesson: Count attackers vs defenders; sacrifice only when 2-3 pieces can join immediately.

moments.mechanism: The g5 knight was pinned on the g-file (Rg4 vs Rg6/Kg7). 28.h4! attacks the pinned piece (about equal); Qf5 lets Black consolidate.
moments.expected_lesson: Attack pinned pieces, especially with pawns.

moments.mechanism: The b3 pawn was defended; Qxb3+ recaptures with check on the a2-g8 diagonal.
moments.expected_lesson: Count defenders before capturing; watch recaptures that come with check.

moments.mechanism: 31...Qxg3# was mate in one.
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: 35...Qe5# was mate in one.
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: Promoting on g1 where the a1 rook covers the square (63.Rxg1 possible). Position stayed winning, so the eval drop is small.
moments.expected_lesson: Before promoting, check what covers the queening square.

moments.mechanism: Caro-Kann vs 3.Nc3: ...c5 (c-pawn moved twice) when the centre is not locked; 3...dxe4 is the main line.
moments.expected_lesson: Identify the structure after move 3 (Advance vs Classical) before choosing ...c5.

moments.mechanism: 14...Nc2 forks the a3 queen and a1 rook.
moments.expected_lesson: Check every square an enemy knight can reach next move.

moments.mechanism: Queen on g2 is deep in enemy camp with few exits; Rhg1 (also after 17...b6) would nearly trap it. 17/18...Qg6 brings it back.
moments.expected_lesson: When your queen raids, count its escape squares every move.

moments.mechanism: Queen on e4 saw the undefended h1 rook down the diagonal: 22...Qxh1.
moments.expected_lesson: After every move, trace your queen's lines to the end.

moments.mechanism: The c5 pawn blocked the g1-a7 diagonal between White's bishop and the b6 queen; capturing with it lets Bxb6.
moments.expected_lesson: If your queen sits on a line with an enemy piece, check what blocks it before moving that blocker.

moments.mechanism: 9.Nc7+ forks king and a8 rook (Nc7+ Kd7 Nxa8).
moments.expected_lesson: Look for knight checks that also attack a rook or queen.

moments.mechanism: 21.Nc6+ forks the king and the d8 rook.
moments.expected_lesson: Check every square an enemy knight can reach next move.

moments.mechanism: Knight retreats to the rim; 13...exf3 14.Rxf3 g4 forks the f3 rook and h3 knight.
moments.expected_lesson: Before retreating to the rim, check pawn forks (pawns attacking two pieces).

moments.mechanism: The g4 pawn was defended by the f6 knight; Nxg4 wins the bishop.
moments.expected_lesson: Count a target's defenders before capturing it.

moments.mechanism: Queen leaves the defense to take b2; 28.Qxe6+ and Qxd5 hit the exposed king.
moments.expected_lesson: Before grabbing material with the queen, check your king without it.

moments.mechanism: d6 looked free, but 16...Ne5! attacks the f3 queen AND uncovers Qd8 onto the d6 knight (the d7 knight was the blocker); after the queen moves, Qxd6.
moments.expected_lesson: Before capturing, look for enemy pieces lined up behind a blocker that can move with a threat.

moments.mechanism: Castling short with White's bishop pinning on g5 and the h-pawn on h4; 10...h6 first was best. Bxc6 bxc6 g4 follows.
moments.expected_lesson: Against a g5 pin plus an advancing h-pawn, ask the bishop with ...h6 before castling.

moments.mechanism: The queen on d8 was the only defender of the d5 knight, which the a2 bishop attacked. After Qh4, Bxd5.
moments.expected_lesson: Ask what the moving piece was defending.

moments.mechanism: The c4 pawn was the only defender of the d5 knight, which the black king on e6 attacked. After c5, Kxd5.
moments.expected_lesson: Pawns are defenders too: ask what a pawn was guarding before pushing it.

moments.mechanism: The d2 bishop was the only defender of the c3 knight (attacked by Bb4). After Bf4, Bxc3 wins the knight and forks the rooks on a1 and e1.
moments.expected_lesson: Ask what the moving piece was defending.

moments.mechanism: The c1 bishop was the only defender of b2 (attacked by the f6 bishop). After Bf4, Bxb2 and Bxa1 wins the exchange and a pawn.
moments.expected_lesson: Ask what the moving piece was defending.

moments.mechanism: The black queen on d2 was attacked by the rook on d1 and nothing defended it. h6 ignores it: Rxd2.
moments.expected_lesson: Before making your own move, ask what the opponent's last move attacks.

moments.mechanism: The bishop on a3 was attacked by the queen on d3 and undefended. Nb4 counterattacks but the queen simply takes: Qxa3.
moments.expected_lesson: Before making your own move, ask what the opponent's last move attacks.

moments.mechanism: The knight on a8 (after taking the rook) was attacked by the a7 queen and undefended. Ba4 leaves it: Qxa8.
moments.expected_lesson: Before making your own move, ask what the opponent's last move attacks.

moments.mechanism: The queen moved to d7, where the e5 knight attacks it: Nxd7.
moments.expected_lesson: Before letting go, check if the destination square is attacked.

moments.mechanism: The knight moved to a5, where the d8 queen attacks it and nothing defends it: Qxa5.
moments.expected_lesson: Before letting go, check if the destination square is attacked and undefended.

moments.mechanism: Nh3 defends the attacked f4 bishop but the knight itself is undefended on h3: Bxh3.
moments.expected_lesson: A move that defends one piece can hang another: check the destination square.

moments.mechanism: The knight gives check on d5, but the e5 queen takes it with check: Qxd5+.
moments.expected_lesson: A check is not safe just because it is a check: is the checking piece defended?

moments.mechanism: Qf3 lets Nd2, a knight fork hitting the f3 queen, f1 rook and c4 bishop.
moments.expected_lesson: Check every square an enemy knight can reach next move.

moments.mechanism: Qd5! attacks the e4 knight and threatens Qxf7# with the c4 bishop at the same time (also hits c5).
moments.expected_lesson: When a queen can threaten mate and a piece at once, the piece usually falls.

moments.mechanism: Qe6+ checks the king on g8 and attacks the c8 rook along the diagonal.
moments.expected_lesson: Before moving, check every enemy check: does any check also hit a loose piece?

moments.mechanism: f6 opens the 7th rank: Qg7+ checks the king and attacks the g4 bishop.
moments.expected_lesson: Before moving, check every enemy check: does any check also hit a loose piece?

moments.mechanism: g3 attacks the queen but Nxg3 fxg3 Qe4+ checks the king and wins the h1 rook along the long diagonal.
moments.expected_lesson: Before attacking a piece, check what checks it gets in return.

moments.mechanism: Capturing with the rook leaves the back rank: Qe6+ Kf8 Qe7+ Kg8 Qe8#. 45...Qxc4+ (with check) was winning.
moments.expected_lesson: When your back rank is weak, recapture with the piece that keeps it covered; prefer captures with check.

moments.mechanism: Bg4 allows a forced mate: Qh4+ f6 Qxf6+ Kc8 Qh8#. 26...Qxf2+ was best.
moments.expected_lesson: Before each move with your king exposed, check every enemy check.

moments.mechanism: 23...Rd2+ Kb1 Qxb2# was mate in 2. Nxe1+ still wins, just much slower.
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: 32...Qf2+ Kxe4 Qd4# was mate in 2; Qxg1 wins material but not the game at once.
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: 37.Rf8+ Kh7 Rh8# was mate in 2 (h6 still mates later).
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: 41.Qg3# was mate in one.
moments.expected_lesson: Before any check, ask: is there a check that is mate?

moments.mechanism: The h3 bishop saw the undefended c8 rook down the diagonal: 27.Bxc8. Still winning after Na7, but a rook less.
moments.expected_lesson: After every move, trace your long-range pieces' lines to the end.

moments.mechanism: The f4 pawn was defended by the d5 knight: Bxf4 Nxf4 loses the bishop. Meanwhile 13.Nxc5 took a free bishop.
moments.expected_lesson: Count a target's defenders before capturing it; list all captures first.

moments.mechanism: Nxf2 was already threatened (the e4 knight and c5 bishop against a pawn only the king defends), forking the d1 queen and h1 rook. d3 does not stop it; 8.O-O did.
moments.expected_lesson: Before making your own move, ask what the opponent threatens.

moments.mechanism: 15...Nfg3+! hxg3 Nxg3+ checks the king on e2 and forks the h1 rook.
moments.expected_lesson: Look for knight checks that also attack a rook or queen, even after a sacrifice.

moments.mechanism: 4...Be6 took the c8 bishop off b7's defense. 5.Bxb7 takes the pawn with the g2 bishop and the a8 rook has no safe square (Nd7 Bxa8). 5.Qb3 hits the same pawn but gives Black a move to defend it (Nd7/Rb8). Only an inaccuracy: Black blundered next move (5...Nc6?, 6.Qxb7).
moments.expected_lesson: When the opponent moves a defender away, check what it was guarding: take it now, before they cover it.
